questions.q: Which should you do first when you find data you want on a website?
options: Start scraping with the fastest loop possible
Check whether an official API or download exists, then review robots.txt and the terms of use
Use a fake User-Agent so the site cannot tell you are a script
Copy the HTML into a DataFrame without reading any rules
questions.explain: An official API or file is more stable and clearly permitted. If you do scrape, check robots.txt and the terms of use first.

options: A legally binding contract between you and the site
A file the site publishes that describes which paths automated tools should or should not fetch; a widely followed convention
A Python module for parsing HTML
A list of the site's API keys
questions.explain: robots.txt is a convention. It is not law and it does not replace the site's terms of use, which may forbid scraping even where robots.txt is silent.

questions.q: In the lesson's code, what does soup.select("article.product_pod") return?
options: The first matching element only
A DataFrame of all products
The site's robots.txt rules
A list of every element that matches the CSS selector (20 product cards on the page)
questions.explain: select returns all matches. select_one returns just the first.

questions.q: After scraping, the price column contains text such as '£51.77'. What is the right next step?
options: Nothing; pandas automatically treats it as a number
Drop the column
Strip the non-numeric characters and convert with pd.to_numeric
Call drop_duplicates on it
questions.explain: Scraped values arrive as text. The cleaning tools from Chapter 5 (str.replace and to_numeric) apply directly.

questions.q: A page's data is added by JavaScript after the page loads. Why might requests.get(url) not find it?
options: requests only receives the initial HTML and does not run the page's scripts
requests cannot make HTTPS calls
Beautiful Soup deletes JavaScript output
The status code is always 404 for such pages
questions.explain: requests downloads the HTML the server sends; content that scripts generate later in a browser is not in that response.
